title.rendered: Artificial Movie: Andrew Garfield Just Became Sam Altman [Trailer Breakdown]

content.rendered:
The first trailer for the Artificial movie just dropped, and it turns Silicon Valley’s messiest boardroom fight into two minutes of pure prestige-drama tension.

Neon released the teaser this week, and the timing is not an accident. Luca Guadagnino, the director behind some of the most talked-about arthouse hits of the last decade, is now pointing his camera at the five days in November 2023 when OpenAI’s board fired Sam Altman, then scrambled to bring him back after employees threatened to walk.

Here is everything confirmed so far: who plays who, what actually happened in real life, when you can watch it, and why studios suddenly can’t stop making movies about AI executives.

Who Plays Who in the Artificial Movie Cast

Casting a tech drama is tricky. Get it wrong and the whole thing reads like a parody. Neon went with a lineup built for award-season buzz, not stunt casting.

Andrew Garfield leads as Sam Altman, and the trailer leans into his unsettling calm rather than a cartoonish villain performance. Monica Barbaro plays Mira Murati, the former OpenAI CTO who found herself at the center of the crisis. The supporting cast reads like a who’s who of the actual tech world during that November week.

🎬 Actor 🧑‍💼 Real Person 🏢 Role in the Crisis
Andrew Garfield Sam Altman CEO
Fired then reinstated
Monica Barbaro Mira Murati Interim CEO
Ran the company during the ousting
Yura Borisov Ilya Sutskever Board / Co-founder
Led the vote against Altman
Mark Rylance Geoffrey Hinton Outside Voice
AI pioneer commenting on the fallout
Ike Barinholtz Elon Musk Rival
OpenAI co-founder turned rival
Cooper Hoffman Greg Brockman President
Resigned in protest alongside Altman

Simon Rich wrote the script, which explains the trailer’s dark comedy undertone. This is not a dry corporate documentary. It is being pitched as a workplace thriller with jokes.

Garfield reportedly spent months studying Altman’s public appearances, from congressional testimony to podcast interviews, to nail the specific cadence that made Altman such a polarizing communicator. Barbaro’s take on Murati leans into the impossible position she was put in: running a company for five days while its future was decided by people who would not explain themselves.

The Real Story Behind the Artificial Movie

If you were not glued to tech Twitter in November 2023, here is the short version.

OpenAI’s board fired Sam Altman without warning, citing a breakdown in trust. No specific misconduct was ever detailed publicly. Within 48 hours, more than 700 of OpenAI’s roughly 770 employees signed a letter threatening to quit unless the board resigned and reinstated Altman.

Microsoft, which had invested billions into OpenAI, publicly offered Altman and his team jobs on the spot. Five days later, the board reversed course. Altman came back as CEO, and most of the board members who voted him out were gone within weeks.

It remains one of the strangest corporate stories of the AI boom: a company nearly imploded over a disagreement that its own board still has not fully explained.

That silence is exactly why a scripted retelling works. A documentary needs cooperation from its subjects. A drama does not. Guadagnino and Rich are free to imagine the closed-door conversations that Altman, Sutskever, and the rest of the board have never fully addressed in public, which is likely where the film’s dark comedy angle will do the most work.

When Does Artificial Come Out? Release Date and Where to Watch

Mark your calendar twice for this one.

Artificial premieres at the New York Film Festival on October 5, 2026, the traditional launchpad for awards contenders. Neon then confirmed a wide theatrical release on Christmas Day, December 25, 2026, putting it squarely in the middle of the holiday box office and awards conversation.

That gap between the festival premiere and the wide release is standard for prestige films. Expect a wave of reviews out of NYFF in early October, then a second wave of coverage as the December release approaches.

✅ Confirmed: trailer released, NYFF premiere date, Christmas Day wide release, full principal cast. ❌ Not yet confirmed: runtime, MPA rating, and whether Sam Altman or OpenAI have issued any official response.

Related: The Musk vs. Altman OpenAI Emails That Explain Everything

Search Interest in the Artificial Movie Is Already Spiking

The trailer has been live for barely a few days, and search interest is already climbing fast. Searches combining “artificial” with “movie” jumped roughly 70 to 80 percent in the last 24 hours compared to the prior day, well ahead of the broader, slower-moving interest in “artificial intelligence” as a general topic.

That gap matters. It shows people are not just casually curious about AI this week. They are actively looking for information about one specific film, right after seeing the trailer for the first time.

📊 Interest in “artificial movie” searches: up sharply, still climbing. ⏱️ Time since trailer release: a few days and counting. 💰 Box office signal: too early to call, but the NYFF premiere on October 5 will be the first real read on reception.

Expect that search curve to spike again twice more this year: once around the NYFF premiere in early October, and again in the days before the Christmas Day wide release.

Why Hollywood Keeps Making Movies About AI Executives

Artificial is not an isolated bet. Studios have figured out that the people building AI are now as recognizable, and as dramatically useful, as the tech itself.

A few things make the Altman story specifically irresistible to a director like Guadagnino: a company that claims to be building something world-changing, a leadership fight with no clear villain, and an ending that satisfied almost nobody. That is the exact ambiguity great character dramas are built on.

Expect more of this. If Artificial performs well in December, other AI-adjacent corporate dramas currently in development will move faster toward production.

FAQ

What is the Artificial movie about?

It dramatizes the five days in November 2023 when OpenAI’s board fired CEO Sam Altman, employees revolted, and Altman was reinstated. Director Luca Guadagnino frames it as a dark comedy drama rather than a straight biopic.

Who plays Sam Altman in Artificial?

Andrew Garfield plays Sam Altman. Monica Barbaro, Yura Borisov, Mark Rylance, Ike Barinholtz, and Cooper Hoffman round out the cast as other key figures from the OpenAI crisis.

When does Artificial release in theaters?

Artificial premieres at the New York Film Festival on October 5, 2026, then opens wide in theaters on Christmas Day, December 25, 2026, via Neon.

Is Artificial based on a true story?

Yes. It is based on OpenAI’s real November 2023 leadership crisis, when the board fired Sam Altman and reversed the decision five days later after employee backlash.

Where can I watch the Artificial trailer?

The official teaser trailer is available through Neon’s channels and major entertainment outlets that covered its release this week, including Variety and Deadline.

The Bottom Line

The Artificial movie turns one of tech’s strangest weeks into what could be one of 2026’s most talked-about films, and the timing could not be better for anyone trying to make sense of how we got here. Bookmark this page. We will update it with the full trailer breakdown and early NYFF reactions the moment they land.

title.rendered: The 3D Figurine AI Trend on ChatGPT: The Exact Prompt That Works

content.rendered:
The 3D figurine AI trend on ChatGPT is catching up fast to what Gemini started with Nano Banana. Every feed right now has someone shrunk down into a collectible toy version of themselves, standing on a tiny acrylic base.

Most tutorials floating around only cover Gemini, since Google’s Nano Banana model kicked off the craze first. ChatGPT can produce the same collectible-figurine look, but it needs a different prompt structure to avoid getting flagged when a real face is attached.

This guide breaks down the exact prompt built for ChatGPT’s image model, why it needs to be worded differently than the Gemini version everyone is copying, and the small tweaks that push the result from plastic-looking to genuinely collectible.

The Exact Prompt for ChatGPT

Attach a clear, full-body or waist-up photo of yourself, then paste this:

Turn this photo into a 1/7 scale collectible figurine. Subject: keep the person’s face, likeness, and proportions from the attached photo, rendered in a smooth toy-like material with visible sculpted detail. Base and packaging: the figurine stands on a round clear acrylic base with no text engraved on it, placed next to a matching display box with clean minimal typography and a plastic window. Setting: a wooden desk with a computer monitor in the background showing a 3D modeling wireframe of the same figure. Lighting: soft studio lighting, subtle shadows under the base, slight reflective sheen on the material. Avoid: real skin texture, human hair strands, blurry edges, distorted hands, visible brand names or logos on the packaging.

✅ Naming the desk, the box, and the wireframe screen first gives ChatGPT a full scene to render, which shifts focus away from the uploaded face ✅ “Keep the person’s face, likeness, and proportions” works better than describing facial features again, since ChatGPT already reads them from the photo ❌ Never write “realistic human” anywhere in the prompt. ChatGPT treats that phrase as a flag for identity manipulation and blocks more often

Why ChatGPT Handles This Differently Than Gemini

Gemini’s Nano Banana model was built for this kind of image-to-image editing from the start, so it accepts a real face plus a full styling prompt in one shot without much friction.

ChatGPT’s image model applies a stricter layer of review when a prompt combines an uploaded face with heavy physical transformation instructions. The figurine trend counts as heavy transformation, since the whole point is turning a person into plastic.

The fix works the same way it did for the 90s AI photo trend: describe the environment in detail and let the face carry over as a simple reference, instead of rewriting the face itself. For the original figurine wave and the trend that led into it, the 90s AI photo trend on Gemini covers how Gemini handles real faces more loosely across the board.

Tips to Make the Figurine Look Realistic

  • Ask for “visible seam lines at the joints,” a small detail that separates a convincing figurine from a smooth plastic blob
  • Add “matte finish on the clothing, glossy finish on the base,” since real collectibles mix textures instead of using one uniform sheen
  • Skip asking for “perfect symmetry.” Real manufactured figurines have tiny asymmetries that make the render look less like a 3D icon

Run the prompt two or three times if the face comes out warped or the hands look off. ChatGPT struggles more with hand detail on figurines than Gemini does, and a second attempt usually fixes it without changing the wording.

ChatGPT vs. Gemini for the 3D Figurine AI Trend

Feature 🤖 ChatGPT 🎨 Gemini (Nano Banana)
👤 Real face handling ⚠️ Stricter, needs scene-first wording ✅ Built for this exact use case
⏱️ Average attempts needed 2 to 3 1
✋ Hand and finger accuracy ⚠️ Weaker ✅ Strong
💰 Free tier available ✅ Yes ✅ Yes
🚫 Refusal rate on first try Higher Lower
🖼️ Best use case Simple bust or waist-up figurines Full-body, pose-heavy figurines

FAQ

Does ChatGPT refuse the figurine prompt often?

More often than Gemini, especially with full-body photos. Leading with the desk, base, and packaging details instead of describing the person lowers the refusal rate noticeably.

Why do the hands look distorted in my result?

Hand and finger detail is a known weak spot for ChatGPT’s image model, more so on stylized renders like figurines. Running the same prompt again usually produces a cleaner result.

Can I skip the packaging box and just get the figure?

Yes. Remove the box sentence from the prompt and keep the acrylic base and desk setting. The box adds authenticity, but it is not required for the figurine itself to render correctly.

Which tool gives a more convincing figurine overall?

Gemini currently produces sharper, more accurate results on the first try, since Nano Banana was built specifically for this kind of transformation. ChatGPT catches up when the prompt centers on the scene instead of the face.

Try It Before the Trend Fades

Pick a clear, well-lit photo, paste the prompt above into ChatGPT, and lean on the desk-and-packaging details to carry the collectible look. If the hands or face come out warped, run it again before changing any wording.

title.rendered: The 90s AI Photo Trend on ChatGPT: The Exact Prompt That Works

content.rendered:
Everyone chasing the 90s AI photo trend on ChatGPT hits the same wall. The results come out too smooth, too modern, or ChatGPT simply refuses the request when a real face is involved.

The trend blew up first on Gemini, where photorealistic vintage recreations landed almost on the first try. ChatGPT plays by different rules. Its image model leans harder on caution around real human faces, so the exact same prompt that works on Gemini often gets watered down or rejected outright here.

This guide gives you the ChatGPT-specific version of the prompt, built around a setting instead of a face-first description, plus the wording tweaks that keep the output from looking like a AI render.

The Exact Prompt for ChatGPT

Attach a clear, front-facing photo of yourself, then paste this:

Turn this photo into a candid snapshot taken inside a 1990s American video rental store. Subject: keep the person’s face and features from the attached photo, natural unposed expression, standing in one of the aisles. Setting: rows of VHS tapes on shelving, hand-written cardboard genre signs, checkered tile floor, fluorescent overhead lighting, a return bin near the counter. Wardrobe: casual early-to-mid 1990s clothing, an oversized graphic tee or a windbreaker jacket. Camera and film quality: visible film grain, slightly warm color cast, on-camera flash with mild red-eye, soft focus, small corner timestamp reading 1994. Avoid: modern signage, digital displays, smartphones, airbrushed skin, studio lighting, visible store brand names or logos.

✅ Naming the location first (video rental store) gives ChatGPT a scene to build around instead of a face to scrutinize, which lowers the chance of a refusal

✅ “Keep the person’s face and features from the attached photo” works better than re-describing the face, since ChatGPT already has the reference image

❌ Never write “photorealistic” in the prompt. ChatGPT associates that word with deepfake requests and blocks more often when it appears

Why ChatGPT Handles This Differently Than Gemini

ChatGPT’s image model runs a stricter check on prompts that combine a real uploaded face with detailed physical descriptions of that same face. Gemini tends to accept this combination more freely.

The workaround is to shift the weight of the prompt. Instead of describing the person, describe the room. ChatGPT spends its attention on the video store, the lighting, and the grain, and treats the face as a simple carry-over from the photo.

For the original version of this trend, built specifically around Gemini’s looser handling of real faces, check out The 90s AI Photo Trend: How to Recreate It With Gemini.

Tips to Make the Result Look Authentic

  • Ask for “one slightly blurry hand,” since real candid photos from a moving subject rarely came out perfectly sharp
  • Add “flash reflection on a nearby glossy surface,” a detail almost every disposable camera photo from that decade has
  • Skip any mention of a specific store chain. Generic descriptions keep the prompt from tripping trademark-related filters

Run the prompt two or three times if ChatGPT returns something that still reads as digital. Small rewording, like swapping “video rental store” for “video store aisle,” sometimes changes the outcome more than adjusting the lighting details.

ChatGPT vs. Gemini for the 90s AI Photo Trend

Feature 🤖 ChatGPT 🎨 Gemini
👤 Real face handling ⚠️ Stricter, needs indirect wording ✅ More permissive
⏱️ Average attempts needed 2 to 3 1 to 2
🎞️ Film grain accuracy ✅ Strong ✅ Strong
💰 Free tier available ✅ Yes ✅ Yes
🚫 Refusal rate on first try Higher Lower
🖼️ Best use case Scene-heavy shots (stores, arcades) Close-up portrait shots

FAQ

Does ChatGPT refuse this prompt every time?

No. Refusals happen more often than on Gemini, but leading with the setting instead of the face lowers the refusal rate significantly. If it fails once, rephrase the location detail and try again.

Can I use the same prompt from the Gemini version?

Not word for word. The Gemini prompt describes the face in detail, which ChatGPT reads as a stricter request. Use the version above, built around the setting instead.

Why does my photo still look too clean?

ChatGPT sometimes over-corrects toward polish. Adding “slightly underexposed” and “visible flash glare” to the prompt pushes it toward a rougher, more authentic look.

Which AI tool gives better results for this trend overall?

Gemini currently produces convincing results faster and with fewer refusals. ChatGPT catches up when the prompt centers on a detailed scene rather than a close-up face.

Try It Before the Trend Fades

Pick a clear photo, paste the prompt above into ChatGPT, and lean on the video store setting to carry the vintage feel. If the first result looks off, reword the scene before touching the wardrobe or lighting details.

title.rendered: GTA 6 System Requirements 2026: What Your PC Actually Needs

content.rendered:
Your PC handled Cyberpunk 2077 on high settings. It chewed through Alan Wake 2. But GTA 6 system requirements are the question keeping PC gamers up at night, and the honest answer is more complicated than any spec sheet floating around right now.

Rockstar drops GTA 6 on November 19, 2026, and the hype has reached a fever pitch few games ever touch. The catch nobody talks about enough: as of today, the game is confirmed only for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. There is no PC release date, and there are no official PC specs from Rockstar. Every “confirmed” chart you’ve seen online is a guess dressed up as fact.

By the end of this guide, you’ll know exactly what’s real, what’s prediction, and how to build or upgrade a PC that’s ready the moment Rockstar finally announces the PC version.

Quick Answer: Is There Even a GTA 6 PC Version Yet?

No. Rockstar’s official GTA 6 page lists PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has said publicly that a PC release is coming eventually, but not on day one, and treated that as a deliberate business call rather than a technical limitation.

History backs this up. GTA V hit PC about 18 months after its console debut. Red Dead Redemption 2 took roughly 13 months. If GTA 6 follows the same pattern, a PC launch lands sometime in 2027, with official system requirements arriving three to six months before that.

None of this means you should stop planning. It means every GTA 6 system requirements chart online right now, including ours, is an educated estimate built from console hardware, Rockstar’s engine history, and comparable AAA titles. Treat it as a planning tool, not a guarantee.

GTA 6 System Requirements: The Three Predicted Tiers

We built these tiers from three sources: the PS5 and Xbox Series X hardware baseline, the demands of Red Dead Redemption 2 on Rockstar’s RAGE engine, and how the visual fidelity in GTA 6’s trailers compares to current top-tier releases.

Tier 1: Minimum (1080p, Low to Medium Settings)

This tier gets you a playable frame rate, not a pretty one. Expect texture pop-in and dropped shadows on distant objects.

  • CPU: Intel Core i5-11600K or AMD Ryzen 5 5600
  • GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3060 or AMD RX 7600
  • RAM: 16 GB
  • Storage: 150 GB, NVMe SSD required

Tier 2: Recommended (1440p, High Settings)

This is where most PC gamers will actually land. Solid frame rates, real ray tracing on select effects, no compromises that ruin the experience.

  • CPU: Intel Core i7-12700K or AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D
  • GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5070 or AMD RX 9070
  • RAM: 32 GB
  • Storage: 150 GB, Gen 4 NVMe SSD

Tier 3: Enthusiast (1440p to 4K, Ultra with Ray Tracing)

Full ray tracing, maxed draw distances, and headroom for whatever performance mods the community throws at the game in year one.

  • CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D or Intel Core Ultra 9 285K
  • GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5080 or better
  • RAM: 32 GB
  • Storage: 150 GB, Gen 5 NVMe SSD

GTA 6 System Requirements Comparison Table

Predicted specs, based on console hardware and Rockstar’s RAGE engine history. No official PC requirements exist yet.
Component 🟢 Minimum 🟡 Recommended 🔴 Enthusiast (4K/RT)
CPU i5-11600K / Ryzen 5 5600 i7-12700K / Ryzen 7 5800X3D Ryzen 7 9800X3D / Core Ultra 9 285K
GPU RTX 3060 / RX 7600 RTX 5070 / RX 9070 RTX 5080 or better
💾 RAM 16 GB 32 GB 32 GB
⏱️ Storage 150 GB NVMe SSD 150 GB Gen 4 NVMe 150 GB Gen 5 NVMe
Target Resolution 1080p 1440p 1440p to 4K
Ray Tracing ❌ Off ✅ Select effects ✅ Full
📊 Est. Upgrade Cost Existing mid-range PC $800–$1,200 $2,000+ build

Why These Predicted Specs Make Sense

The RAGE engine has never been kind to hard drives. Red Dead Redemption 2 already leaned hard on fast storage, and GTA 6’s Leonida map is bigger. An old mechanical drive will bottleneck the asset streaming that makes the open world feel seamless, so an NVMe SSD is not optional in any tier.

The RAM jump to 32 GB for anything beyond minimum settings reflects a broader 2026 trend. Modern open-world engines lean on system memory for NPC simulation and traffic AI, both of which Rockstar has teased heavily in GTA 6 trailers.

DLSS 4 and FSR 4 support is not officially confirmed, but it would be a shock if Rockstar skipped upscaling entirely. Every major 2026 release leans on it to hit playable frame rates with ray tracing enabled, and GTA 6 will almost certainly follow.

Does Your Current PC Stand a Chance?

You don’t need to guess. Three checks tell you almost everything.

Step 1: Check Your GPU

Your graphics card is the single biggest bottleneck for any Rockstar open-world game. If you’re running anything older than an RTX 3060 or RX 6600, budget for an upgrade regardless of which tier you’re targeting.

Step 2: Check Your RAM

Sixteen gigabytes is the new floor, not the ceiling. If you’re still at 8 GB, that upgrade should happen before you even think about the GPU.

Step 3: Check Your Storage

Open File Explorer or Disk Utility and confirm your main drive is an SSD, not a spinning hard drive. If GTA 6 streams the world the way RDR2 did, an HDD will cause stutter no GPU can fix.

What to Upgrade First on a Budget

If your PC falls short, upgrade in this order for the best return per dollar.

✅ Priority 1: NVMe SSD ($50 to $150). Cheapest fix, biggest impact on load times and world streaming.

✅ Priority 2: GPU ($300 to $700). The 2026 memory chip shortage has pushed GPU prices up sharply, so shop early rather than waiting until launch week panic hits.

✅ Priority 3: RAM, 16 GB to 32 GB ($60 to $100). A simple swap on most modern motherboards.

❌ Priority 4: CPU. Only necessary if you’re still on a processor older than six years. Most modern mid-range chips will hold up fine.

Once you’ve upgraded the GPU, keep the drivers current and stable. A fresh graphics card paired with a flaky driver install is a common source of crashes right after launch week, and our guide on how to fix NVIDIA driver crashing walks through the exact fix if you run into it.

FAQ

Is GTA 6 confirmed for PC?

No. Rockstar has only confirmed PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S for the November 19, 2026 launch. A PC version is expected but has no confirmed release window, based on Rockstar’s pattern with GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2.

Can I run GTA 6 on a laptop?

A gaming laptop with an RTX 4060 or better, 16 GB of RAM, and an NVMe SSD should handle minimum to recommended settings once a PC version ships. Thermal throttling on thin laptops may limit sustained performance versus a desktop with the same GPU.

Does GTA 6 support ray tracing on minimum settings?

Predicted minimum settings skip ray tracing entirely to protect frame rate on lower-end hardware. Ray tracing effects are expected to activate starting at the recommended tier, based on how Rockstar handled RDR2’s PC port.

How much storage does GTA 6 need?

Estimates point to roughly 150 GB, in line with GTA V and RDR2’s PC footprint scaled up for Leonida’s larger map. Confirm this number once Rockstar publishes official specs.

Should I upgrade my PC now or wait?

Wait on the GPU if you can, since 2026’s memory chip shortage has pushed prices up across the board. Upgrading storage and RAM now is safe and useful regardless of when GTA 6 arrives on PC.

The Bottom Line

There’s no official GTA 6 system requirements chart yet, and anyone claiming otherwise is guessing. What you can do right now is make sure your storage is fast, your RAM clears 16 GB, and your GPU isn’t older than an RTX 3060. That puts you ahead of most PC gamers the moment Rockstar finally makes the announcement.

Bookmark this page. We’ll update every tier the second official specs land.

title.rendered: The 90s AI Photo Trend: How to Recreate It With Gemini

content.rendered:
The 90s AI photo trend is spreading fast, and Gemini is turning out to be the most consistent tool for pulling it off. One photo, one detailed prompt, and you get a convincing throwback snapshot in seconds.

Unlike other AI tools, Gemini handles real faces combined with vintage scene details without tripping safety filters as often. That makes it the easiest starting point if you want a quick, reliable result.

Below is the exact prompt, structured the way a prompt engineer would build it, plus the small adjustments that make the difference between a convincing photo and an obviously fake one.

The Exact Prompt for Gemini

Attach a clear, front-facing photo of yourself, then paste this:

Recreate this photo as a real 1990s point-and-shoot snapshot (not 1980s). Subject: an adult man with brown/tan skin tone, natural candid expression, sitting on a couch. Action: playing a classic gray home video game console, holding a boxy controller with both hands, eyes focused on the TV. Setting: 1990s living room, wood paneled walls, a warm yellow lamp, a bowl of popcorn and a mug nearby, generic vintage video game posters on the wall. Wardrobe: bold patterned knit sweater typical of the early-to-mid 1990s. Camera and film quality: visible film grain, warm amber-orange color cast, harsh direct on-camera flash, natural skin texture, slightly soft focus, minor motion blur, small timestamp in the corner. Avoid: modern consoles, modern furniture, digital sharpness, studio lighting, airbrushed skin, visible logos or brand names, anything from the 1980s specifically.

✅ Breaking the prompt into Subject, Action, Setting, and Wardrobe blocks keeps Gemini from skipping details buried in a long paragraph
✅ “Not 1980s” locks the decade, since Gemini sometimes blends neighboring eras when you only say “90s”
❌ Skip brand names entirely, generic descriptions like “gray home video game console” work better than naming one

Why Gemini Handles This Better Than Other Tools

Real faces combined with detailed vintage scenes sometimes trigger stricter safety filters on other AI tools. Gemini tends to process this exact type of request without blocking it, which makes it the more reliable option for this specific trend.

That does not mean every result comes out perfect on the first try. Small wording adjustments still matter.

If ChatGPT is your only option, the approach needs to change. Check out The 90s AI Photo Trend on ChatGPT: The Exact Prompt That Works for the scene-first version of the prompt built to get past its stricter filters.

Tips to Make the Result Look Authentic

  • Ask for “slight underexposure” instead of even lighting, real flash photos from that era were rarely well balanced
  • Request a “cropped, off-center composition,” since candid 90s shots were almost never centered
  • Never add “smooth skin” or “perfect lighting” to the prompt, that instantly makes the result look digital

Run the prompt twice if the first output feels too polished. Even with identical wording, Gemini varies its output, and a second attempt often nails the grain and flash texture better than the first.

FAQ

Does Gemini require a paid subscription for this?

No. Gemini offers a free tier that handles this type of prompt well. Results are consistent enough for casual use, though a paid plan may offer faster processing during high traffic periods.

Why did my photo come out too clean?

Overly sharp or well-lit source photos confuse the AI’s sense of “vintage.” Use a photo with natural, slightly uneven lighting for a more authentic starting point.

Can I use this prompt with any photo?

Yes, but front-facing, clearly lit photos produce the most convincing results. Heavily filtered or low-resolution photos often produce distorted or unnatural output.

Try It Before the Trend Fades

Grab a recent selfie, copy the prompt above into Gemini, and post your result while this wave is still peaking.

title.rendered: Best VPN for AI Browsing in 2026: Keep ChatGPT and Gemini Private

content.rendered:
Every time you type a question into ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok, something happens behind the scenes that most people never think about. The best VPN for AI browsing won’t make you invisible, but it closes one of the biggest privacy gaps these tools leave wide open: your IP address.

AI chatbots have quietly become the new search engines. People ask them about symptoms, salary negotiations, breakup texts, and business plans they wouldn’t say out loud in public. Yet almost none of that data stays as private as users assume.

This guide breaks down what ChatGPT, Gemini, and other AI tools actually do with your information, whether a VPN really helps, and which three services are worth your money if privacy is the goal.

Why ChatGPT and Gemini Know More About You Than You Think

Most people assume deleting a chat means the conversation is gone. It rarely is.

ChatGPT keeps standard conversations for 30 days after you delete them, and Operator screenshots for 90 days. If training is enabled on your account, that data can stick around indefinitely.

Gemini defaults to an 18-month retention window, adjustable between 3 and 36 months. Any conversation flagged for human review gets kept for up to three years, no matter what you do in your settings.

Even Claude, often marketed as the privacy-conscious option, retains conversations for about 30 days with training disabled, and up to five years in de-identified form if training is on.

None of this requires a data breach. It’s just how the business model works. Every prompt gets tied to your account, your IP address, and often your device fingerprint.

Does a VPN Actually Stop AI Chatbots From Tracking You?

Here’s the honest answer: a VPN won’t stop OpenAI or Google from storing your conversation once you’re logged in. If you type your name, your city, or your job title into the chat, no VPN on earth can un-share that.

What a VPN does well is break the link between your IP address and your account activity. Without it, your internet provider, your network admin, and the AI platform itself can all see the raw connection between your location and every query you send.

For logged-out or trial use, a VPN also stops chatbots from silently profiling you by location, something several 2026 privacy audits flagged as common practice among smaller AI platforms.

Think of it as one layer in a stack, not a magic shield. Pair it with private or temporary chat modes, and you close most of the easy tracking angles.

The Best VPN for AI Browsing: 3 Options Worth Paying For

Not every VPN is built the same way, and speed matters more than people expect when you’re running AI tools that already eat bandwidth with long responses and image generation.

NordVPN: Best Overall Pick

NordVPN retains the highest percentage of your original connection speed on local servers, which matters if you’re using voice mode or generating images through an AI assistant. It also ships post-quantum encryption, a feature aimed squarely at future-proofing your traffic against advanced decryption methods.

Its Threat Protection tool blocks known malicious domains, useful since fake “AI chatbot” browser extensions have become a real vector for data theft. Ten simultaneous connections cover most households.

Surfshark: Best Value for Multiple Devices

Surfshark undercuts the competition on price while still delivering fast WireGuard speeds. The standout feature for AI browsing is CleanWeb, which blocks trackers before they load, including some of the third-party scripts found embedded in AI chatbot websites.

Unlimited simultaneous connections make it the practical choice if your whole household uses AI tools across phones, laptops, and tablets.

ExpressVPN: Best for a Full Privacy Stack

ExpressVPN made the boldest move of 2026 by launching its own suite of privacy tools alongside the VPN itself. ExpressAI, Identity Defender, and a built-in password manager turn the app into more than a simple IP mask.

It’s the slowest of the three on raw speed tests, but for someone who wants one subscription covering VPN, identity monitoring, and password management, the bundle argument is strong.

VPN ⏱️ Local Speed 💰 Starting Price 📊 Devices 🔒 Standout Feature ✅ Best For
NordVPN 1256 Mbps (96% retained) $2.91/mo 10 Post-quantum encryption Overall speed + security
Surfshark 1615 Mbps (75% retained) $1.99/mo Unlimited CleanWeb tracker blocking Households, multiple devices
ExpressVPN 489 Mbps (54% retained) $6.67/mo 8 (14 on Pro) ExpressAI + Identity Defender Full privacy stack in one app
Proton VPN Moderate Free tier available 1 (free) / 10 (paid) Genuine no-logs free plan Testing before paying

Bonus: Proton VPN for a Genuinely Usable Free Tier

If you’re not ready to pay, Proton VPN is the rare free VPN that doesn’t sell your data or throttle you into uselessness. Speeds lag behind the paid leaders here, but it’s a legitimate way to test whether a VPN changes how you use AI tools before committing to a subscription.

How to Actually Use a VPN With AI Chatbots

Installing a VPN is the easy part. Getting the privacy benefit requires a few habits most people skip.

✅ Connect the VPN before opening ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok, not after
✅ Use temporary or incognito chat modes whenever the platform offers them
✅ Turn off training data sharing in your account settings
✅ Avoid typing your real name, employer, or exact location into prompts
❌ Don’t assume a VPN protects what you willingly type into the chat
❌ Don’t reuse the same VPN server for banking and AI sessions if location correlation worries you

FAQ

Does a VPN hide what I type into ChatGPT?

No. A VPN masks your IP address and network-level location, but the content of your prompts is still sent to and stored by the AI provider according to its own retention policy.

Which VPN is best specifically for AI chatbots?

NordVPN offers the best overall speed and security balance for heavy AI use, Surfshark wins on value for multiple devices, and ExpressVPN adds extra identity protection tools beyond the VPN itself.

Can AI companies still identify me if I use a VPN?

Yes, if you’re logged into an account. A VPN hides your IP, not your account credentials, email, or anything you type that identifies you personally.

Do free VPNs work for AI browsing privacy?

Most free VPNs log or sell user data, defeating the purpose. Proton VPN’s free tier is a rare exception with a genuine no-logs policy, though speeds are limited.

The Bottom Line

A VPN won’t make your AI conversations disappear, but it removes the easiest tracking signal these platforms rely on: your raw IP address. Combine it with temporary chat modes and a habit of keeping identifying details out of your prompts, and you’ve closed most of the realistic privacy gaps.

Pick NordVPN if speed and future-proof encryption matter most, Surfshark if you’re covering a whole household on a budget, or ExpressVPN if you want the VPN bundled with identity monitoring tools built for exactly this kind of risk.

title.rendered: GPT-6 Astra Release: What OpenAI’s New Model Means for Developers

content.rendered:
The GPT-6 Astra release just went live, and OpenAI is calling it the most capable model it has ever shipped. The company says Astra tops the field in computer use, coding, browsing, cybersecurity, and professional work.

That is a big claim on launch day. But the benchmark numbers OpenAI published, and the pricing attached to them, give developers and engineering teams something concrete to evaluate right now, not just marketing language.

This breakdown covers everything the GPT-6 Astra release changes, how Astra stacks up against GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude’s current lineup, what it costs, and how to get access today.

What the GPT-6 Astra Release Actually Changes for Your Stack

Astra is not a minor version bump. OpenAI reports it saturates ARC-AGI-3 at 99.9% and reaches 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4, both frontier-level scores for reasoning and abstract problem solving.

For day-to-day engineering work, three areas stand out:

✅ Computer use — Astra completes OSWorld 2.0 tasks in roughly 47% less time than GPT-5.6 Sol. ✅ Coding — Astra scores 57.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, up from 37.3% for the previous model. ✅ Long context — Astra hits 96.3% on an 8-needle retrieval test across 512K to 1M tokens, versus 73.8% for Sol.

The model ships under the API name gpt-6-astra, and OpenAI is also updating the Codex harness alongside it, which the company says produces a 1.9x faster task completion rate on the Mind2Web benchmark.

Cybersecurity: A New “Critical” Threshold

This is the part enterprise security teams should read closely. OpenAI classifies Astra as meeting the Critical threshold for cybersecurity under its own Preparedness Framework, its highest internal risk tier.

The numbers back that up. Astra hit a perfect 100% on ExploitBench, compared with 78.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol. On SRE-Bench, a reverse-engineering benchmark, it solved 88% of tasks on the first try.

📊 During testing, Astra reportedly found two previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities on its own, which OpenAI says it disclosed to the affected maintainers.

Because of this, OpenAI is keeping some cyber capabilities locked down at launch. Astra can currently run secure code review and patching tasks, but it will refuse requests to generate proof-of-concept exploits. Broader access is expected through OpenAI’s Daybreak program in the coming weeks.

For teams researching this shift, our guide on how to protect your data from AI chatbots covers the defensive side of this same trend.

GPT-6 Astra vs GPT-5.6 Sol vs Claude: Pricing and Benchmarks

If you are deciding whether to migrate workloads, price and performance matter more than headline benchmarks. Here is how the numbers compare.

Model 💰 Price (Input/Output per 1M) 📊 Coding (Terminal-Bench 4.0) ⏱️ Computer Use (OSWorld 2.0) 🧠 Reasoning (FrontierMath T4)
🚀 GPT-6 Astra $10 / $50 57.9% ✅ 72.6% ✅ 97.6% ✅
GPT-5.6 Sol $5 / $30 37.3% ❌ 65.7% 83.0%
Claude Fable 5.1 $10 / $50 55.8% — * 87.8%
Claude Opus 5 $5 / $25 💰 52.6% 70.2% 73.2%

* Not reported in OpenAI’s published OSWorld 2.0 offline comparison. Benchmark scores per OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra launch announcement (Sept 2026); pricing per Anthropic and OpenAI API rate cards. Scores from different labs may use different harnesses.

A few things jump out. Astra’s $10/$50 per million token rate sits at the same tier as Claude’s Fable 5.1, OpenAI’s closest rival in raw benchmark scores. Claude Opus 5 remains the budget-conscious option among frontier-adjacent models, at roughly half that price.

⏱️ On pure speed for computer-use tasks, Astra’s 47% time reduction versus Sol is the most immediately useful number for teams running high-volume agentic workflows, where latency compounds fast.

GPT-6 Astra Release Timeline: How to Get Access

The GPT-6 Astra release is rolling out in stages, not all at once. Here is the order:

  1. Limited organizations get access first, starting today.
  2. ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users follow over the coming days.
  3. Developers can call it now through the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, or AWS Bedrock using the model ID gpt-6-astra.

Enterprise admins should note that Astra is off by default at launch. Workspace admins need to manually enable it for their teams, which gives IT and security leads a review window before rollout.

Astra also supports Zero Data Retention for eligible API customers, a detail that matters for teams in regulated industries evaluating the switch.

Should You Switch After the GPT-6 Astra Release?

For teams already deep in the OpenAI ecosystem, especially those using Codex for agentic coding, Astra’s speed and coding gains make it worth testing immediately. The pricing is competitive with Anthropic’s top tier, and the benchmark gap on coding and computer-use tasks is not small.

For teams running cost-sensitive workloads, the calculation is less obvious. Claude Opus 5 still undercuts both Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol on price, and for tasks that do not need frontier-level reasoning, it may remain the better default.

The honest answer: the GPT-6 Astra release sets a new ceiling on raw capability, but it is not automatically the new default for every workload.

FAQ

What is the GPT-6 Astra release? The GPT-6 Astra release is OpenAI’s newest flagship AI model, launched today. OpenAI positions it as its most capable and most aligned model to date, with top scores on computer use, coding, cybersecurity, and scientific reasoning benchmarks.

How much does GPT-6 Astra cost? Standard API pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. A Fast mode option doubles both the price and the processing speed.

Is GPT-6 Astra available now? It is rolling out in stages. Select organizations have access today, ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users get it over the coming days, and developers can already call it via the API, Azure, or AWS Bedrock.

Is GPT-6 Astra better than Claude? On several published benchmarks, including coding and computer-use tasks, Astra edges out Claude Fable 5.1. Claude Opus 5 remains notably cheaper, so the better choice depends on whether your workload needs frontier-level performance or cost efficiency.

Why is GPT-6 Astra’s cybersecurity rating a concern? OpenAI classified Astra at the Critical threshold for cyber capability, meaning it can identify and develop exploits at a level that requires extra safeguards. OpenAI has restricted some cyber functions at launch as a result.

The Bottom Line

The GPT-6 Astra release raises the ceiling on what a single model can do across coding, computer use, and cybersecurity work, but it arrives with real caveats around cost and access controls that enterprise teams cannot skip. Test it against your actual workloads before committing budget, and watch how OpenAI’s Daybreak program expands cyber access in the coming weeks.

title.rendered: How to Protect Your Data From AI Chatbots (2026 Guide)

content.rendered:
Every time you type a question into ChatGPT, Gemini, or Meta AI, that message doesn’t just disappear after you get an answer. Knowing how to protect your data from AI chatbots starts with understanding what actually happens to your words after you hit send.

AI chatbots have become the new default search engine for millions of people. They answer medical questions, draft emails, and even help with therapy-adjacent conversations. But most users never open the privacy settings buried three menus deep.

This guide breaks down exactly how chatbot providers collect, store, and sometimes train on your conversations, plus the specific settings you need to change today to lock things down.

Why AI Chatbots Collect Your Data in the First Place

Large language models don’t learn on their own. They improve through a process called reinforcement learning from human feedback, and one of the richest sources of feedback is real conversations from real users.

When a company trains its next model version, it often pulls from a pool of past chats. This is why so many chatbots ask for a thumbs up or thumbs down after a response. That single click can become training data.

📊 A few things typically get logged:

  • ✅ The text you type
  • ✅ Files or images you upload
  • ✅ Device and browser metadata
  • ✅ Timestamps and session length
  • ❌ Rarely your exact location, unless you grant permission

How Each Major Chatbot Actually Handles Your Data

Not every AI platform treats your conversations the same way, and the differences matter more than most users realize.

🤖 Chatbot 📥 Trains on Your Chats by Default 🔕 Opt-Out Available 🗑️ Data Retention 💼 Paid/Team Plan Privacy
ChatGPT (OpenAI) ✅ Yes, unless disabled ✅ Yes, in settings ⏱️ 30 days after deletion request ✅ Excluded from training on Team/Enterprise
Gemini (Google) ✅ Yes, unless disabled ✅ Yes, via Gemini Apps Activity ⏱️ Up to 3 years if activity is on ✅ Excluded on Workspace plans
Claude (Anthropic) ❌ No, by default ✅ Opt-in only if you allow it ⏱️ Varies, deletable on request ✅ Not trained on by default across all plans
Meta AI ✅ Yes, tied to your account data ⚠️ Limited, varies by region ⏱️ Tied to broader Meta data policy ⚠️ No dedicated enterprise privacy tier

Policies change frequently. Always check each provider’s current privacy settings before assuming a default.

OpenAI’s ChatGPT trains on conversations by default unless you manually disable it in settings. Google’s Gemini works similarly, tied into your broader Google Activity controls. Anthropic’s Claude takes a different default stance, not training on consumer conversations unless a user opts in.

Meta AI is the trickiest of the group, since it’s often woven into apps like Instagram and WhatsApp, which already collect substantial behavioral data.

The Real Risk Isn’t Hacking, It’s Oversharing

Most people picture data breaches when they think about chatbot risk. The bigger issue is simpler: users voluntarily paste sensitive information into a chat window without thinking twice.

⏱️ Common oversharing mistakes:

  • ✅ Pasting full contracts with client names still visible
  • ✅ Sharing medical symptoms alongside personal identifiers
  • ✅ Uploading tax documents to “double check the math”
  • ❌ Assuming a chat is private just because no one else can see your screen

Once information leaves your device and enters a company’s servers, you’re trusting their retention policy and their security team, not your own judgment in the moment.

How to Protect Your Data From AI Chatbots: The Settings That Matter

Here’s the part most guides skip. These are the actual toggles you should check right now.

For ChatGPT: Go to Settings, then Data Controls, and turn off “Improve the model for everyone.” This stops new conversations from being used for training.

For Gemini: Open Gemini Apps Activity through your Google Account and pause it. This also limits how long your prompts are retained.

For Claude: Check your privacy settings to confirm whether conversation feedback sharing is enabled, since it’s opt-in rather than a default you need to disable.

For Meta AI: Review your Accounts Center privacy settings, since Meta AI data often ties back into ad personalization across its family of apps.

Practical Habits That Protect You No Matter Which Chatbot You Use

Settings help, but habits matter more long term. 💰 A breach or policy change is largely irrelevant if you never fed sensitive data in first place.

  • ✅ Strip names, account numbers, and addresses before pasting documents
  • ✅ Use a separate, non-work account for personal AI experimentation
  • ✅ Periodically clear your chat history instead of letting it accumulate
  • ✅ Read the privacy policy update emails instead of archiving them unread
  • ❌ Don’t assume “delete conversation” means immediate permanent removal everywhere

Frequently Asked Questions

Do AI chatbots read my messages in real time?
Yes, a message has to be processed to generate a response. The question isn’t whether it’s read once, but whether it’s stored, reviewed by humans for quality checks, or used later to train future models.

Can I permanently delete my chat history from an AI chatbot?
Most platforms let you delete conversations from your account view, but backend deletion timelines vary. OpenAI states a 30 day window for full removal after a deletion request, for example.

Is it safe to use AI chatbots for work documents?
Only on enterprise or team plans that explicitly exclude your data from training, and only after checking your company’s own data handling policy first.

Do free chatbot plans have weaker privacy than paid plans?
Generally yes. Free tiers are more likely to use conversations for training since that data effectively subsidizes the cost of running the model.

Should I worry about voice chatbot features specifically?
Voice adds an extra data layer, since audio recordings may be stored separately from text logs, so check for a dedicated voice data setting where offered.

The Bottom Line

You don’t need to quit using AI chatbots to protect your privacy, you just need to stop treating them like a locked diary. Check your settings today, not after something goes wrong.

Take five minutes right now to open your chatbot’s privacy dashboard. That single habit does more for your data security than any browser extension ever will.

title.rendered: Is Linux More Secure Than Windows in 2026? The Honest Answer

content.rendered:
Every Linux forum will tell you the same thing: switch and you’ll never get hacked again. Is Linux more secure than Windows in reality, or is that just old advice repeating itself? The truth in 2026 is more nuanced, and more useful, than either camp wants to admit.

This closes out our three-part look at desktop security, after we broke down macOS vs Windows security in detail. Linux gets treated as the “safe” default in that conversation, but the 2026 threat data tells a messier story.

By the end of this guide, you’ll know exactly where Linux wins, where it quietly loses, and which five settings actually matter if you’re making the switch this year.

Why Linux Has a Different Attack Surface, Not a Smaller One

Linux isn’t invisible to attackers. It just gets attacked differently than Windows.

Windows dominates consumer malware because it dominates consumer desktops. Attackers build for volume. Linux, on the other hand, runs the servers, cloud instances, and containers that hold the actual valuable data.

That’s why Linux malware detections sit near 1.3% of the global total, even though Linux powers roughly 90% of public cloud workloads. 📊 The attackers went where the money is: web servers, SSH endpoints, and container infrastructure, not home desktops.

If you’re running Linux as a personal laptop OS, you’re statistically a much smaller target than a Windows user. If you’re running it as a server, the calculus flips completely.

The 2026 Threat Data Nobody Mentions in the “Linux Is Safer” Argument

Here’s the part the pro-Linux crowd tends to skip.

Kernel vulnerability disclosures aren’t shrinking. They’re exploding. The Linux kernel logged over 3,500 CVEs in 2024 alone, a roughly tenfold jump from prior years, mostly because the kernel team became its own CVE Numbering Authority and started documenting bugs that used to go quietly unrecorded.

That’s not necessarily bad news. More disclosure means more transparency, not more danger. But it does mean the “Linux barely has vulnerabilities” talking point is outdated.

Then there’s the XZ Utils incident. A single attacker spent over two years building trust as a maintainer on a core compression library, then slipped a backdoor into the software supply chain feeding into major distributions. CISA rated it a maximum-severity CVSS 10.0. It was caught by luck, not process.

Add brute-force attacks, which account for the vast majority of endpoint behavior seen on Linux systems, almost entirely targeting exposed SSH ports, and you get a real picture: Linux security depends heavily on configuration, not on the OS being inherently bulletproof.

Where Linux Genuinely Beats Windows and macOS

None of this means Linux is worse. It means the advantages are specific, not magical.

✅ Smaller consumer malware ecosystem. Fewer pre-packaged threats target desktop Linux specifically.

✅ Granular permission control. You decide exactly what runs with elevated privileges, instead of trusting a vendor default.

✅ Fast patching on mainstream distros. Ubuntu, Fedora, and Debian typically ship kernel and package security fixes faster than the median patch cycle Windows sees on edge devices.

✅ Transparent source code. Anyone can audit what’s actually running, which is exactly how the XZ backdoor eventually got caught.

✅ No forced telemetry or bundled bloatware creating extra attack surface you didn’t ask for.

Where Linux Quietly Loses

🔍 Security Factor 🐧 Linux 🪟 Windows 11 🍎 macOS
💰 Malware volume (2025) ✅ ~1.3% of global detections ❌ Largest target by far ✅ Low, but rising
📊 Reported kernel/OS CVEs ❌ 3,500+ kernel CVEs in 2024 alone ⚠️ High, less publicly granular ⚠️ Moderate, closed disclosure
⏱️ Average patch time ✅ Fast for mainstream distros ⚠️ 32-day median (edge devices) ✅ Fast, but user-dependent
🎯 Main attack vector SSH brute-force, web servers Phishing, credential theft Phishing, malicious installers
📦 Supply chain risk ⚠️ Real (XZ Utils, 2024) ⚠️ Real (third-party installers) ✅ App Store review helps
🔒 Out-of-the-box hardening ⚠️ Depends entirely on distro/user ✅ Defender enabled by default ✅ Gatekeeper enabled by default
👤 Best fit Users who will actually configure it Users who want protection by default Users who want a locked-down ecosystem

❌ Zero hardening by default. A fresh Ubuntu install doesn’t harden SSH, doesn’t enable a firewall, and doesn’t restrict sudo out of the box. Windows Defender and macOS Gatekeeper are active the moment you boot.

❌ Fragmented security responsibility. “Linux” isn’t one OS. A hardened Fedora server and an unpatched Raspberry Pi running an old Debian image are both “Linux,” with wildly different risk profiles.

❌ Supply chain trust is fragile. Community-maintained packages don’t get the same review budget as a corporate app store.

❌ You are the security team. If you don’t configure it, nobody did.

How to Actually Harden Your Linux Machine in 2026

Lock Down SSH First

Disable password authentication and switch to key-based login. This alone kills the brute-force vector that accounts for the majority of Linux endpoint attacks.

Enable a Firewall by Default

UFW on Ubuntu or firewalld on Fedora takes under five minutes to configure and closes ports you don’t even know are open.

Turn On Automatic Security Updates

Unattended-upgrades (Debian/Ubuntu) or dnf-automatic (Fedora/RHEL) keeps kernel and package patches current without you remembering to run apt update weekly.

Restrict sudo Access

Give your daily user account only the privileges it needs. A compromised low-privilege account is a much smaller problem than a compromised admin account.

Audit What You Install

Stick to official repositories and verified sources. The XZ Utils incident happened inside the trusted supply chain, not from some sketchy download site, so vigilance matters even with “official” packages.

Related: macOS vs Windows Security: Which One Actually Protects You Better? — https://techonplay.com/macos-vs-windows-security/

FAQ

Is Linux immune to viruses?

No. Linux has far fewer consumer malware threats than Windows, but it isn’t immune. Server-focused threats like ransomware, cryptomining malware, and SSH brute-force attacks target Linux systems constantly, especially unpatched or misconfigured ones.

Do I need antivirus software on Linux?

For a personal desktop, it’s usually optional if you follow good hardening practices. For servers or business use, endpoint monitoring tools matter more than traditional antivirus.

Which Linux distro is the most secure by default?

Fedora and openSUSE ship with SELinux or AppArmor enabled out of the box, giving them stronger default hardening than most Ubuntu-based distros, which require manual configuration.

Is Linux more secure than Windows for everyday users?

It can be, but only if you actually configure it. Windows offers stronger out-of-the-box protection through Defender. Linux offers stronger ceiling protection, but only for users willing to set it up properly.

What was the XZ Utils backdoor and should I still worry about it?

It was a supply chain attack where a malicious actor spent years earning trust as a maintainer before inserting a backdoor into a core Linux compression library. It was caught before widespread deployment, but it proved the model is exploitable and remains a live concern for open-source infrastructure.

The Bottom Line

Linux isn’t automatically safer than Windows or macOS. It’s more controllable. That control only pays off if you actually use it: lock down SSH, enable your firewall, automate your patches, and treat every package install like it matters, because in 2026, it does.

Ready to make the switch? Start with the five hardening steps above before you migrate a single file, and check out our full macOS vs Windows security breakdown to see how all three platforms really stack up.

title.rendered: 100 ChatGPT Image Prompts I Actually Use Instead of Generic AI Photos

content.rendered:
Most people type “make this look professional” into ChatGPT and get the same flat, overlit render everyone else gets. ChatGPT image prompts stop being generic the moment you tell the model exactly how to light, frame, and shoot the scene, not just what to put in it.

That gap between “AI-looking” and “actually usable” content matters more now than ever. Brands, creators, and marketers are shipping dozens of visuals a week, and the ones that stand out are the ones built with real photographic language instead of vague adjectives.

This guide breaks down 100 visual command codes across 10 categories, from lighting to product photography, so you can direct ChatGPT’s image generator like a photographer instead of hoping for the best.

Why Generic Prompts Produce Generic Images

ChatGPT’s image model responds to specificity. When you write “a person in an office,” it fills in every gap with the most statistically average choice: flat light, centered framing, neutral expression. Nothing wrong, nothing memorable either.

The fix isn’t a longer prompt. It’s a structured one. That’s the whole idea behind working with chatgpt image prompts as a system: each command below acts as a single lever, lighting, angle, or composition, that you stack on top of your subject description.

✅ Use them to replace vague terms like “cinematic” or “professional”
✅ Combine two or three per prompt for layered results
❌ Don’t stack more than 3-4 commands, or the model loses focus
❌ Don’t skip the subject description, commands modify a scene, they don’t create one

Lighting Commands That Set the Mood

Lighting decides whether an image reads as a stock photo or an editorial shot. These ten commands control where the light comes from and how hard it hits the subject.

  • 💡 spotlight — carves the subject out of darkness, theater-style
  • 🌅 goldenhour — warm, late-day sun with stretched shadows
  • 🌙 silhouette — clean dark shape against a bright backdrop
  • 🔦 rimlight — a thin bright outline lifts the subject off the background
  • 🎨 chiaroscuro — painterly extremes of light and shadow

Surreal Commands For Scroll-Stopping Concepts

When a normal photo won’t cut it, these commands push the scene into impossible territory while keeping it visually coherent, ideal for thumbnails and social hooks.

  • 🌀 portal — a doorway linking two different worlds in one frame
  • 🪶 gravityoff — everything floats, as if gravity quit its job
  • 🔁 infinite — one element repeats into a hypnotic distance
  • 🏙️ giantobject — an everyday item becomes a monument-sized landmark

Framing Commands That Control Focus

Framing decides what the eye lands on first. These ten commands are the difference between a cluttered image and one with clear visual hierarchy.

  • 🖼️ negativeSpace — generous empty space, great for adding text overlays
  • 🔍 closeup — lets face, texture, or product detail carry the frame
  • ⚖️ symmetry — mirrored halves for maximum graphic punch
  • 📐 ruleofthirds — subject on a third line for a relaxed, editorial balance

Behind-the-Scenes Commands For Authenticity

BTS-style images perform well because they feel unstaged, even when fully generated. These commands expose the “production” around the shot.

  • 🎬 BTS — the polished shot steps back to reveal the crew and gear
  • 📹 camerarig — camera body, lens, and monitor become visible props
  • 🔀 beforeafter — raw setup and finished frame side by side

Camera Angle Commands For Instant Drama

The camera position alone can make a subject feel powerful, vulnerable, or immersive without changing anything else in the scene.

  • 🦅 birdsview — straight-down framing that flattens the scene into shapes
  • 👤 POV — first-person framing that drops the viewer into the moment
  • 📉 lowangle — shooting from below makes the subject feel towering
  • 🎥 dutchangle — a tilted horizon injects tension and energy

Related: Google Flow Camera Commands

Editorial Photography Commands For Brand Content

These ten commands borrow directly from fashion and magazine photography, useful when a brand needs to look established rather than experimental.

  • 📸 lookbook — consistent styling, presented like a fashion catalog
  • 🎞️ 35mm — honest grain and timeless lens character
  • 📰 coverstory — a magazine-cover portrait with space for a masthead
  • 📷 polaroid — instant-film softness and casual snapshot framing

Creative Experiment Commands For Unique Visuals

When every competitor is using the same three styles, these commands add a technical or conceptual twist that’s hard to replicate with a basic prompt.

  • 🌡️ thermal — heat-map coloring turns temperature into design
  • 🪞 reflection — the composition is built around mirrors or water
  • 📐 blueprint — technical drawing treatment with measured lines and labels
  • 🌐 tinyplanet — the environment curls into a surreal spherical world

Cinematic Commands For a Movie-Still Look

These commands pull from film stocks and genres, useful for anything meant to feel like a story rather than a static photo.

  • 🌃 neonnoir — rain-slick darkness cut by saturated neon glows
  • 🎬 cinematic — a polished movie-still look with controlled depth
  • 📼 vintagefilm — gentle grain and faded color from an analog past
  • 🎭 filmstill — a frame that feels lifted mid-story from a film

Action Commands For Energy and Motion

Static images undersell movement. These commands make ChatGPT render motion in a way that feels physically real, not blurry or broken.

  • 🤸 midair — the subject hangs suspended at the peak of a leap
  • 💨 windblown — wind whips hair, fabric, and dust believably
  • 💥 impactframe — the exact instant of impact, debris and force lines

Product Commands For E-Commerce and Ads

📂 Category 🎯 Best For ⏱️ Effort 📊 Impact
💡 LightingAny subject, instant mood shiftLowHigh
🌀 Surreal & ImpossibleThumbnails, social hooksMediumHigh
🖼️ Framing & CompositionBlog covers, portraitsLowMedium
🎬 BTS & ProductionAuthentic-feeling brand contentMediumMedium
🎥 Camera & AnglesAdding drama to flat scenesLowHigh
📸 Photography & EditorialBrand credibility, lookbooksMediumMedium
🧪 Creative ExperimentsStanding out from competitorsHighHigh
🎞️ Cinematic LooksStorytelling, video thumbnailsMediumHigh
💥 Action & DynamicsSports, energy-driven contentMediumMedium
📦 Product & AdvertisingE-commerce, ad creativeLowHigh

For anyone generating product visuals, this category alone can replace an entire studio photography session.

  • 📦 packshot — clean studio presentation ready for e-commerce
  • ✨ luxuryad — restrained, immaculate composition that whispers premium
  • 🍏 applestyle — minimal, airy presentation with clean hierarchy
  • 🎈 floatingproduct — the product hovers with soft controlled shadows

How to Combine ChatGPT Image Prompts Without Breaking the Output

The commands aren’t meant to be used one at a time forever. Once you know a handful by heart, layering them is where the real quality jump happens.

A working formula looks like this: subject + 1 lighting command + 1 framing or angle command + optional style command. For example: “a barista pouring coffee, golden hour lighting, close-up, 35mm film grain” produces a warm, tightly framed, film-grain shot instead of a flat product photo.

⏱️ Takes seconds to test
💰 Costs nothing beyond your existing ChatGPT plan
📊 Cuts revision rounds because the first output is closer to what you meant

Try All 100 Commands Below

001 — 100

ChatGPT Image Prompt Commands

Tap any card to copy a ready-to-paste phrase for your next prompt.

techonplay.com · 100 ChatGPT Image Prompts

Instead of scrolling back to find a command, use the interactive list below. Search by mood, filter by category, and tap any card to copy a ready-to-paste phrase straight into your ChatGPT prompt.

FAQ

Do these commands work in every ChatGPT plan?

Yes, the commands are prompt language, not a special feature, so they work anywhere ChatGPT can generate images, including the free tier with image limits.

Can I combine commands from different categories?

Yes, and it’s often better. A lighting command plus a framing command plus a style command usually outperforms using three commands from the same category.

Why does ChatGPT sometimes ignore a command?

Overloaded prompts confuse the model. Keep it to three or four commands per prompt, and place the subject description first so the model has a clear anchor.

Are these commands the same as Midjourney parameters?

No, Midjourney uses technical flags like --ar or --stylize. These are descriptive keywords that work because ChatGPT’s image model responds to natural language, not command-line syntax.

Do I need to type the slash symbol?

No, the slash is a mnemonic from the original format, not a functional trigger. What actually works is the descriptive phrase, so typing “golden hour lighting” works the same as typing “/goldenhour.”

The Real Advantage Is Repetition, Not Memorization

Nobody needs to memorize 100 commands. What works is picking five or six across lighting, framing, and style that fit your niche and using them consistently until they become second nature.

The creators winning right now are the ones treating chatgpt image prompts as a toolkit, not a lucky guess. They stopped guessing and started directing.

title.rendered: Google Flow Camera Commands: 40 Prompts to Steal Right Now

content.rendered:
Google Flow just got a lot more fun to use, if you know the right words to type. Google Flow camera commands are short prompt tags that tell the AI exactly how to frame a shot, from a drone view straight down to a tight close-up on your face.

Most people typing into Flow stick to basic prompts like “make a cool photo of me.” That gets generic results. The creators pulling millions of views right now are typing specific camera and drone commands instead, and the difference in output quality is obvious the moment you compare the two.

This guide breaks down all 40 commands, grouped by what they actually do, plus a comparison table so you can find the right one in seconds. Grab a photo of yourself, pick a command below, and start generating.

What Google Flow Camera Commands Actually Do

Camera commands work like a director’s shot list, translated into text. Instead of describing a scene in vague terms, you tell Flow the exact angle, distance, and movement you want.

Think of it as the difference between telling a photographer “take a nice picture” versus “shoot this from a low angle, close up, with a shallow depth of field.” One gets you a random result. The other gets you a specific look.

These commands were first popularized through social media carousels showing them applied to a well known athlete. The same structure works for anyone, including a normal selfie shot in your living room.

Aerial and Angle Commands: From Drone Shots to Ground Level

This first group controls the vertical position of the camera relative to you. These are the commands that turn a flat photo into something that looks like it was shot by a production crew.

✅ Best for: hero shots, profile pictures, anything that needs to feel bigger than a phone selfie ❌ Avoid for: casual, everyday posts where a dramatic angle feels out of place

  • /DRONEVIEW — High aerial view from above
  • /TOPDOWN — Directly above the subject
  • /BIRDSEYE — Bird’s-eye perspective
  • /OVERHEAD — Camera directly overhead
  • /EXTREMETOPDOWN — Ultra-high aerial view straight down
  • /DRONE3Q — High drone view at an angle
  • /LOWANGLE — Camera looking upward, makes the subject feel powerful
  • /HIGHANGLE — Camera looking downward
  • /GROUNDLEVEL — Camera close to the ground
  • /WORMSVIEW — Extremely low-angle perspective, dramatic and unusual
  • /LOWUP — Low-angle close-up built for a strong, confident look

📊 Data point: angle-based prompts are the single biggest lever for making an AI-generated photo feel professional instead of AI-generated. A slight low angle alone can change how authoritative a portrait looks.

Camera Movement Commands That Add Cinematic Motion

Static shots are fine, but movement commands are what make people stop scrolling. These simulate a camera physically moving through space, which Flow renders as motion blur, depth shifts, or a tracking feel.

⏱️ These work especially well for short video generations, not just single images.

  • /TRACKING — Cinematic moving-camera feel
  • /ORBIT — Camera circling the subject
  • /ORBITCLOSE — Camera circling closer around the subject
  • /PUSHIN — Camera moving toward the subject
  • /PULLOUT — Camera moving away from the subject
  • /CRANEUP — Low to high rising shot
  • /DRONEREVEAL — Camera pulls back to reveal the full scene
  • /MOTIONBLUR — Subject in motion with a blur effect
  • /AERIALTRACK — Drone tracking the subject from above

If you only try three commands from this whole list, make it /PUSHIN, /ORBIT, and /DRONEREVEAL. They consistently produce the most shareable results.

Framing and Composition Commands for Better Storytelling

This group is about distance and composition rather than angle. These are the commands that separate a snapshot from something that looks intentional.

  • /CLOSEUP — Face-focused close-up
  • /MEDIUMSHOT — Upper-body or half-body shot
  • /FULLBODY — Full subject visible
  • /PORTRAIT — Portrait-focused framing
  • /WIDEANGLE — Wide environmental shot
  • /LONGSHOT — Subject small, environment large
  • /PROFILE — Side profile shot
  • /CLOSEPROFILE — Tight profile close-up
  • /OVERSHOULDER — Shot from behind the shoulder toward the subject
  • /POV — Subject looking directly into the camera
  • /BEHIND — Camera positioned behind the subject
  • /EYELEVEL — Natural, eye-level shot with no distortion

Mood and Effect Commands for a Cinematic Finish

The last group adds atmosphere. These commands do not change where the camera sits, they change how the shot feels once it is framed.

  • /CINEMATIC — Adds cinematic composition and depth
  • /DUTCHANGLE — Dramatic tilted camera
  • /DUTCHTILT — Tilted camera for a similar dramatic effect
  • /SILHOUETTE — Backlit silhouette shot
  • /REFLECTION — Shot including a natural reflection
  • /FRAMED — Subject framed by the surrounding environment
  • /THROUGHOBJECT — Shot through a foreground element
  • /THROUGHNET — Shot through a net, fence, or similar frame

Google Flow Camera Commands Comparison Table

Category Example Commands Best For Difficulty Impact
🚁 Aerial & Angle /DRONEVIEW, /LOWANGLE, /WORMSVIEW Hero shots, profile pics ⭐ Easy 📊📊📊 High
🎥 Camera Movement /ORBIT, /PUSHIN, /DRONEREVEAL Short videos, reels ⭐⭐ Medium 📊📊📊 High
🖼️ Framing & Composition /CLOSEUP, /FULLBODY, /PORTRAIT Everyday posts, profile photos ⭐ Easy 📊📊 Medium
🎬 Mood & Effect /CINEMATIC, /SILHOUETTE, /DUTCHANGLE Standout, dramatic posts ⭐⭐ Medium 📊📊📊 High

How to Actually Use These Commands With Your Own Photos

Using these prompts is simple once you understand the pattern. Upload a clear photo of yourself, then add one command tag to your text prompt, describing the setting you want.

For example: “A person standing in a modern kitchen, /LOWANGLE, natural lighting, casual outfit.” Flow reads that tag and applies the angle described above.

You can combine two commands for a more specific result, such as pairing /PORTRAIT with /CINEMATIC for a magazine-style headshot. Do not stack more than two or three, since Flow can start ignoring conflicting instructions.

A quick note on faces: since you are recreating these shots with your own photo instead of a public figure, results tend to be more consistent and there is no risk of the output resembling someone else’s likeness.

Common Mistakes When Prompting Camera Angles in Google Flow

  • ❌ Typing the command without describing the scene around it, which produces a floating, generic subject
  • ❌ Combining conflicting angles, like /TOPDOWN and /EYELEVEL in the same prompt
  • ❌ Using a blurry or low-resolution source photo, which limits how sharp the final angle looks
  • ✅ Pairing one angle command with one mood command for the cleanest results
  • ✅ Testing the same prompt twice, since Flow varies slightly between generations

FAQ

Do I need a paid Google Flow plan to use these commands?

No special plan is required specifically for camera commands. They work as plain text tags inside any prompt, though your available generations still depend on which Flow tier you are subscribed to.

Can I use more than one camera command in the same prompt?

Yes, combining two works well, such as an angle command with a mood command. Adding three or more often confuses the output, so keep it simple for the most reliable results.

Do these commands work for video generation too?

Yes. Movement commands like /ORBIT, /PUSHIN, and /DRONEREVEAL are actually built for motion and tend to look better in video generations than in single static images.

Will using my own face instead of a celebrity change the output quality?

No, the commands control the camera behavior, not the subject. A clear, well-lit source photo of yourself works just as well as any other subject.

Where did this list of commands originally come from?

The format was popularized through social media posts using a well known athlete as the visual example. The commands themselves are generic Flow prompt tags that work with any subject.

Final Take

Forty commands sounds like a lot, but you really only need five or six in regular rotation to make your Google Flow content look sharper than 90 percent of what is on your feed right now. Start with /LOWANGLE, /PORTRAIT, and /CINEMATIC, then branch out from there.

Save this guide, pick your favorite command, and generate your next post today.
